e.etymology: A modern spelling of Kaleah or Kalea with the Kh- of Khloe. Kalea is a Hawaiian name read as the joy; Kaleah also works as an American blend of Ka- and Leah.

e.meaning: little fierce one (Irish); or little Laurence (English)
e.etymology: A respelling of Larkin, an Irish surname from Ó Lorcáin, descendant of Lorcán, little fierce one, and an English surname from a medieval pet form of Laurence.
Arabic madiha, praiseworthy or commendable, from madh, praise.
A modern American coinage that fits Z onto the sound of Dylan and Kylen.
Arabic murtada, the one found pleasing or chosen. Al-Murtada is a title of Ali, the Prophet Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law, which makes the name a favorite in Shia families.
A modern American coinage that blends Anaya or Ana with Ayla and the -la ending of Kayla.

e.meaning: short form of several names; in Yoruba, mercy
e.etymology: Several unrelated names: an Indian short form of Anuradha, Anurag and others; a Yoruba short form of Anuoluwa, God's mercy; and a Finnish pet form of Anna. Anu was also the Mesopotamian sky god.
A Caribbean Spanish elaboration of Ariel, Hebrew for lion of God, with the -ys ending common in Cuban, Dominican and Puerto Rican names.
In the US mostly a girls' name among Zomi (Chin) families from Myanmar, where Niang is a common element of women's names. Niang is also a Senegalese surname.
A respelling of Jameson, an English surname meaning son of James. James is the English form of Jacob, the Hebrew name traditionally read as supplanter.
From Arabic asad, lion, a traditional name and a byname of Ali ibn Abi Talib, called the Lion of God. Assad is the same name with a doubled s.
e.note: In the news Assad means the family that ruled Syria from 1971 to 2024, Hafez and Bashar al-Assad.

e.etymology: The French short form of Sebastien. Sebastian comes from Latin Sebastianus, a man from Sebaste, a city named with the Greek word sebastos, venerable.
An American elaboration of Olivia with the -anna ending. Olivia comes from Latin oliva, olive, and was popularized by Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
A recent Latino coinage that reads as Erick with the initial Y favored in Caribbean and Latin American naming.
A respelling of Galilea, the Spanish and Latin name of Galilee, the region of northern Israel where Jesus grew up. The Hebrew name, Galil, means district or circle.
A respelling of Soraya, the Persian form of Arabic Thurayya, the name of the Pleiades, the cluster of stars in Taurus.
A modern American coinage that joins the Zy- beginning to the -mir sound of Amir and Jamir.
From iyari, the word for heart in the Huichol (Wixarika) language of western Mexico, where it also stands for inherited memory and feeling. Used in Mexico and by Mexican American families.
A respelling of Calliope, in Greek Kalliope, from kallos, beauty, and ops, voice. Calliope was the Muse of epic poetry.
A respelling of Naia or Nyah. Naia is linked to the naiads, the water nymphs of Greek myth, and to nai'a, the Hawaiian word for dolphin.
Created for Padme Amidala in the Star Wars prequels, which began in 1999. It draws on Sanskrit padma, lotus, as heard in the Buddhist mantra om mani padme hum.
namesakes: Padme Amidala (queen and senator in the Star Wars prequels, played by Natalie Portman)

assoc.t: Padme Amidala, Star Wars queen and mother of Luke and Leia

e.etymology: A respelling of Castiel, the angel played by Misha Collins on the TV series Supernatural from 2008. The name is usually traced to Cassiel, an angel of Jewish and Christian lore.

assoc.t: Castiel, the angel on TV's Supernatural

e.etymology: A respelling of Kinsley, an English surname from a Yorkshire place name. The place was a woodland clearing belonging to a man named Cyne, a short form of Old English names meaning royal.
From Sanskrit mayukha, a ray or beam of light, used in India as a girls' name.
From Malibu, the beach city west of Los Angeles. Its name comes from Humaliwo, a Chumash village whose name is usually translated as where the surf sounds loudly.

assoc.t: beach city in Los Angeles County, California

e.etymology: The English adjective elysian, from Elysium, the paradise of Greek myth where heroes rested after death. A recent word name.
Latin noctis, of the night, from nox, night. It came into use as a boys' name through Noctis Lucis Caelum, the prince who leads the 2016 video game Final Fantasy XV.

assoc.t: Noctis, hero of the video game Final Fantasy XV

e.etymology: In Turkish, sevi is a word for love and is used as a girls' name. American use may have other sources as well.
A short name with several sources. For girls it is Marathi ovi, a traditional verse form; for boys it is a Faroese form of Danish Ove or a short form of Ovidiu and Ovidio.
The spelling of Laena Velaryon, a dragonrider in George R. R. Martin's Fire and Blood and the 2022 HBO series House of the Dragon. It also reads as a variant of Lena or Laina.

assoc.t: Laena Velaryon of House of the Dragon

e.etymology: From the Welsh word emyr, ruler or king, known from Emyr Llydaw, a legendary Breton prince of the 6th century. In the US it also serves as a spelling of Emir, the Arabic title for a prince or commander.
